A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VGCURE benchmark and MCDGRAPH framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 14 LVLMs, MCDGRAPH fine-tuning experiments, downstream results, and appendix robustness analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds component-ablation results and error-frequency analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed masked graph infilling, contrastive graph discrimination, and graph description tasks retain the same procedures, inputs, outputs, and equations (1)–(3). The new component-removal variants are experimental controls rather than revisions to MCDGRAPH.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 22-task VGCURE coverage, ten graph structures, VisionGraph, FACTKG, ScienceQA, AOKVQA, and visual-style and naming scenarios. The new analyses use existing QA coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 7 adds three comparison variants that omit masked infilling, contrastive discrimination, or graph description. The original LVLM benchmark, backbone-LLM comparisons, and downstream comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces component-removal controls evaluated on Qwen2-VL QA samples in Section 5.2. Existing benchmark metrics, zero-shot procedures, and main training settings are retained. The PDFs do not specify whether ablation training data or budgets were equalized.

E4.justification: v3 adds the first systematic ablation of all three MCDGRAPH training tasks. Section 3.6 also extends v2's qualitative error taxonomy with category frequencies and task-specific error patterns. These substantially expand component validation and failure diagnosis; the existing robustness analyses and case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new ablation scores and descriptive error percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation or reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the 17 matched original tables are unchanged. New results include 54% relation misunderstanding and 17% structural hallucination in Table 5. Table 7 reports task-dependent ablation outcomes, including NNu accuracy of 2.00 without description versus 98.34 for full MCDGRAPH, and CP EM_F1 of 24.61 without masked infilling versus 11.95 for the full method.

T1.justification: The task equations, mathematical specifications, and graph-generation definitions are retained. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs, and v3 introduces no new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: VGCURE evaluates fundamental graph abilities, LVLMs struggle with structural information, and three-task MCDGRAPH improves graph performance and generalization. New analyses support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the ablations as showing complementary abilities supplied by the three training tasks, while acknowledging improvements after some task removals. It also discusses causes of error prevalence. Existing graph-complexity, model-scale, and general-VQA-transfer limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the training prompts, 10,000/5,000/5,000 sample allocation, LoRA hyperparameters, and four 80GB A100 GPUs. Code and dataset access statements are unchanged. No separate implementation or budget details accompany the new ablations.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds a focused discussion of six GNN-benchmark works, including Open Graph Benchmark, Wiki-CS, TUDataset, and Long Range Graph Benchmark, distinguishing their scope from VGCURE. Some introductory and metric citations are also added or replaced; the existing multimodal-graph positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Error definitions move from Appendix C.2 into new Section 3.6, with added analysis. v3 also adds ablation and GNN-benchmark paragraphs, renames Question-based Answering to Entity-based Answering, changes Normal VQA to General VQA, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. Most prose and the overall organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds error-frequency Table 5 and ablation Table 7, with selected ablation scores highlighted in red. Existing tables and figures are redistributed and tables renumbered; all 25 figure contents are retained. The overall two-column presentation remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's qualitative error taxonomy and absence of component ablations, v3 supplies useful evidence about failure prevalence and dependence on individual training tasks. This improves diagnostic transparency. However, mixed ablation outcomes and missing error-sample size, ablation budget controls, and uncertainty reporting limit the strength of the new complementarity interpretation.
